clownfish.definition: A small fish from warm oceans that lives beside sea anemones and is often kept in home fish tanks.
clownfish.exampleUsage: The clownfish swam beside a sea anemone.

angelfish.definition: A deep-bodied fish with tall fins; marine species are common around tropical reefs.
angelfish.exampleUsage: The angelfish's deep body and tall fins were visible.

pufferfish.definition: A fish of the pufferfish group, known for inflating its body; many species contain powerful toxins.
pufferfish.exampleUsage: The recorded observation shows the pufferfish inflating its body.

lionfish.definition: Brightly striped fish of the tropical Pacific having elongated spiny fins.
lionfish.exampleUsage: The lionfish's long fin spines were visible in the reference.

swordfish.definition: A large sea fish with a long pointed upper jaw.
swordfish.exampleUsage: The swordfish has an elongated upper jaw.

seahorse.definition: A small fish of the genus Hippocampus, with a horse-like head and usually an upright swimming posture.
seahorse.exampleUsage: The seahorse swam upright beside the vegetation.

eel.definition: A long, narrow fish that resembles a snake and lives in water.
eel.exampleUsage: The eel moved through a narrow opening.

manta-ray.definition: A very large ray with broad triangular fins that feeds mainly by filtering tiny organisms from water.
manta-ray.exampleUsage: The manta ray glided with its broad fins extended.

stingray.definition: Large venomous ray with large barbed spines near the base of a thin whiplike tail capable of inflicting severe wounds.
stingray.exampleUsage: The stingray moved across the sandy tank bottom.

piranha.definition: A South American freshwater fish known for its sharp teeth.
piranha.exampleUsage: The piranha swam within the freshwater exhibit.

barracuda.definition: Any voracious marine fish of the genus Sphyraena having an elongated cylindrical body and large mouth with projecting lower jaw and long strong teeth.
barracuda.exampleUsage: The barracuda's long body was visible through the viewing panel.

catfish.definition: A fish of the catfish group, commonly with whisker-like barbels around the mouth; habitats vary by species.
catfish.exampleUsage: The catfish used its barbels while exploring the bottom.

dolphin.definition: A toothed-whale marine mammal of the dolphin group in this animal context.
dolphin.exampleUsage: The dolphin surfaced to breathe air.

whale.definition: A very large marine mammal that breathes air through a blowhole.
whale.exampleUsage: The whale breathed through its blowhole at the surface.

sea-lion.definition: A marine mammal with external ear flaps and strong flippers that can move on land as well as swim.
sea-lion.exampleUsage: The sea lion rested on a platform.

seal.definition: A flippered marine mammal commonly called a seal.
seal.exampleUsage: The seal moved from the water onto the resting area.

walrus.definition: Either of two large northern marine mammals having ivory tusks and tough hide over thick blubber.
walrus.exampleUsage: The walrus's long tusks were visible in the reference.

beluga-whale.definition: A small white toothed whale of Arctic and sub-Arctic waters, known for a rounded forehead.
beluga-whale.exampleUsage: The beluga whale surfaced for air.

orca.definition: Predatory black-and-white toothed whale with large dorsal fin.
orca.exampleUsage: The orca swam with its tall dorsal fin above the surface.

manatee.definition: Sirenian mammal of tropical coastal waters of America.
manatee.exampleUsage: The manatee fed on aquatic vegetation.

narwhal.definition: Small Arctic whale the male having a long spiral ivory tusk.
narwhal.exampleUsage: The reference shows a male narwhal with a long spiraled tusk.

sea-otter.definition: A marine mammal with dense fur that often floats on its back and feeds on shellfish and other sea animals.
sea-otter.exampleUsage: The sea otter floated on its back.

jellyfish.definition: A gelatinous aquatic cnidarian, commonly with a bell-shaped body and tentacles.
jellyfish.exampleUsage: The jellyfish drifted with its tentacles trailing below.

octopus.definition: A marine mollusk with eight arms and a soft body.
octopus.exampleUsage: The octopus moved its eight arms across the rocks.

squid.definition: A marine mollusk commonly with eight arms and two longer feeding tentacles.
squid.exampleUsage: The squid extended its two long feeding tentacles.

starfish.definition: A marine echinoderm, also called a sea star, usually with arms radiating from a central body.
starfish.exampleUsage: The starfish moved across the tank floor using its tube feet.

sea-urchin.definition: A small round marine animal with a hard shell covered in movable spines.
sea-urchin.exampleUsage: The sea urchin was visible among the rocks.

lobster.definition: A large sea animal with a hard shell and two strong claws.
lobster.exampleUsage: The lobster gripped material with its large claws.

crab.definition: A crustacean commonly with a broad body, ten legs and claws on the front pair.
crab.exampleUsage: The crab moved sideways across the sand.

shrimp.exampleUsage: The shrimp swam near the vegetation.
shrimp.definition: A small sea animal with a curved body, many legs, and a hard shell.

anemone.definition: A soft-bodied marine animal with tentacles around its mouth, often attached to a surface.
anemone.exampleUsage: The anemone remained attached to the rock.

sea-cucumber.definition: A soft elongated marine animal related to starfish and sea urchins.
sea-cucumber.exampleUsage: The sea cucumber rested on the aquarium floor.

nautilus.definition: A sea animal with tentacles and a coiled, chambered shell.
nautilus.exampleUsage: The nautilus moved with its chambered shell behind its tentacles.

coral.definition: An animal of the coral group, commonly forming colonies; many kinds build hard skeletons.
coral.exampleUsage: The coral colony grew on the reef structure.

coral-reef.definition: A rigid calcium carbonate framework, built from coral skeletons, provides the reef with its physical structure.
coral-reef.exampleUsage: The coral reef supports many different animals.

kelp-forest.definition: A thick growth of kelp spreads across shallow coastal waters, creating an underwater habitat that resembles a forest.
kelp-forest.exampleUsage: Fish swam through the dense kelp forest.

tide-pool.definition: A small pool of seawater left among rocks when the tide goes out.
tide-pool.exampleUsage: The tide pool retained seawater after the tide went out.

deep-sea.definition: The dark, cold parts of the ocean far below the sunlit surface waters.
deep-sea.exampleUsage: The deep sea lies far below the sunlit surface zone.

tropical-tank.definition: An aquarium tank maintained for species from warm tropical waters.
tropical-tank.exampleUsage: The tropical tank is managed for its specified warm-water species.

freshwater-tank.definition: An aquarium tank containing non-salty water for freshwater species.
freshwater-tank.exampleUsage: The freshwater tank contains non-salty water for its resident species.

mangrove.definition: A tropical tree or shrub bearing fruit that germinates while still on the tree and having numerous prop roots that eventually form an impenetrable mass and are important in land building.
mangrove.exampleUsage: The mangrove grew along the coastal water's edge.

shipwreck.definition: The remains of a vessel damaged, stranded or sunk.
shipwreck.exampleUsage: The exhibit recreates part of a shipwreck on the seafloor.

cave.definition: A geological formation consisting of an underground enclosure with access from the surface of the ground or from the sea.
cave.exampleUsage: The underwater cave has a narrow entrance in the rock.

open-ocean.definition: The broad, deep sea beyond the coastal waters, where land is far from view.
open-ocean.exampleUsage: The species account describes movement through the open ocean.

glass-tunnel.definition: A transparent enclosed walkway that lets visitors pass through or beneath an aquarium exhibit.
glass-tunnel.exampleUsage: Visitors walked through the glass tunnel beneath the exhibit.

touch-pool.definition: A shallow supervised aquarium exhibit where visitors may be allowed to gently touch selected animals under staff rules.
touch-pool.exampleUsage: Visitors followed staff instructions at the touch pool.

viewing-window.definition: A transparent panel through which visitors can observe an aquarium tank or enclosure.
viewing-window.exampleUsage: Visitors watched the fish through the viewing window.

tank.definition: A container of water used to keep aquatic animals.
tank.exampleUsage: The tank holds water for the managed exhibit.

filter.definition: A device that removes selected material from aquarium water.
filter.exampleUsage: The filter removes selected material from the circulating water.

pump.definition: A machine that circulates water through an aquarium.
pump.exampleUsage: The pump circulates water through the system.

lighting.exampleUsage: Staff adjusted the lighting for the exhibit's requirements.

feeding-station.definition: A designated area where aquarium staff provide food to animals under controlled care routines.
feeding-station.exampleUsage: Staff prepared food at the feeding station.

exhibit-sign.definition: A sign that gives visitors information about an exhibit, species, or rule.
exhibit-sign.exampleUsage: The exhibit sign gives the animal's habitat information.

gift-shop.definition: A shop selling souvenirs or items suitable as gifts.
gift-shop.exampleUsage: The visitor bought a souvenir at the gift shop.

ticket-counter.definition: A staffed counter where visitors buy, collect, or ask about admission tickets.
ticket-counter.exampleUsage: The visitor collected admission tickets at the ticket counter.

guided-tour.definition: A planned visit to a place or institution led by a guide who explains what participants are seeing.
guided-tour.exampleUsage: The guided tour explained three separate habitats.
